headline: High: transformers can read/write and browse broadly, while the paired audio-speech agent has no isolation or provenance controls, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A has no documented IO surfaces, but Agent B can read files, run browsers, and process stdin/stdout, so if A’s outputs are bridged into B via files or pipeline, B may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking or isolation, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF A's output is copied into a file or stdin consumed by B
IF B parses A-produced text as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Disable automatic piping between A and B
Insert a manual review step before B consumes A output
Use a strict output schema for A
Run B in a separate workspace
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all handoffs

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read and write the filesystem and has broad network egress, while A has no documented network egress and no data classes touched. If they share a workspace, B can exfiltrate files that A produces or consumes. The lack of documented isolation makes shared-data leakage plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF A and B share a filesystem or workspace
IF B is allowed to send file contents over the network
mitigations: Separate their working directories
Block B from reading A's output directory
Disable B network egress for shared runs
Store sensitive inputs outside the shared workspace
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent sandboxing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has unrestricted filesystem write plus subprocess and shell execution, while A’s profile does not show compensating locking or concurrency controls. If both touch the same directory, B can overwrite or race with A’s artifacts, and the absence of documented coordination makes the conflict dangerous by default.
conditions: IF A and B write to the same directory
IF B modifies files that A later reads without locks
mitigations: Give each agent a separate output directory
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Run only one writer at a time
Make B read-only on A-owned paths
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can ingest files and act on them with shell, browser, and subprocess capabilities, so A’s outputs can become authoritative inputs unless explicitly verified. A has no documented verification or citation controls, and B’s pipeline-style tooling increases the chance that an error in A propagates into downstream actions.
conditions: IF B consumes A output without a verification step
IF B uses A-produced text to drive browser or shell actions
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B acts
Add a validation step between A and B
Constrain B to read-only summarization
Log and diff A outputs before reuse
requires-engineering: implement typed handoff contracts

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and A touches no data classes while B’s data classes are generic multimodal types. The pairwise compliance risk is therefore limited to undocumented deployment choices rather than an inherent mismatch.
conditions: IF deployment assigns regulated data to B
IF A and B are configured under different retention or residency policies
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Document retention settings for both agents
Keep residency settings aligned
Review logs for sensitive content
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement
